title: Aft Fuselage Lower Shell Skin Panel — External Doubler Repair
abstract: Permanent external doubler repair for impact or corrosion damage in the aft fuselage lower shell skin, restoring the skin load path and the external smoothness class in a ground damage prone area.

sections.purpose: This repair restores the static strength and the residual fatigue capability of the aft fuselage lower shell skin after removal of impact or corrosion damage, in the area below the aft belly fairing where ground equipment contact is common.
sections.damage_assessment: Establish the extent of the damage by detailed visual inspection followed by ultrasonic thickness measurement over a radius of at least 200 mm. Damage that stays inside the allowable limits below may be blended out and left unrepaired, with the blend recorded. Damage that crosses a stringer, that reaches a frame foot, or that lies within 60 mm of an existing repair, is outside the scope of this repair. Where the damage is corrosion, remove all product before you measure, because the residual thickness under a corrosion scab is always less than it appears. Record the position against the nearest frame and stringer.
sections.repair_procedure: Remove the damaged material by routing to a smooth oval with a minimum corner radius of 15 mm and blend the edges to the taper on the repair drawing. Do a dye penetrant inspection of the routed edge and an ultrasonic thickness check of the surrounding skin. Cut the external doubler CIN87555-80 to the layout of the repair drawing and drill the fastener pattern using the doubler as a template, keeping the pitch and edge distance given. Where the repair crosses a splice, add the internal doubler D5331120951225 as a packer on the inner face so that the fastener grip stays inside the range on the drawing. Deburr, apply the surface protection of the standard practice to all new surfaces and install the doubler wet with sealant using rivets AES990489-7D on the outer two rows, with washers AGS334024-84 at the inner face where called for. Restore the external finish to aerodynamic smoothness class B and fair the doubler edge with the approved filler. Restore the external paint scheme and the conductivity of the lightning protection across the repair.
sections.inspection_requirements: The repair is life limited to 18 000 flight cycles from the date of embodiment. Do a repeat detailed visual inspection of the doubler perimeter at every heavy check and an ultrasonic inspection of the routed edge every 5 000 flight cycles. Any disbond of the sealant line or any new indication at the routed edge invalidates the repair. Report the repair to Aeralis so that it is recorded against the aircraft.

type_data.allowable_damage_limits: Dents up to 3 mm deep with a diameter above 40 mm and no sharp edge, or corrosion up to 10 per cent of the local skin thickness over an area not exceeding 2 500 square millimetres. One area per skin bay.

repair_drawings.title: External doubler, aft fuselage lower shell skin

type_data.fastener_pattern: Two rows of 56 rivets AES990489-7D at 24 mm pitch and 18 mm edge distance, staggered, with a third row added where the repair crosses a splice
type_data.fatigue_life_note: Repair is life limited to 18 000 flight cycles; ultrasonic inspection of the routed edge every 5 000 flight cycles.

abstract: Permanent external doubler repair for impact or corrosion damage in the aft fuselage lower shell skin, restoring the skin load path and the external smoothness class in a ground damage prone area.

That offset is a design case and not a deviation: the shell as repaired is the datum for any subsequent drain line work in the bay, and no concession is required for an aircraft that carries this repair. Declare the repair when a drain line assembly is ordered for the bay.
